data.exact_reserve_text: The development of insurance liabilities provides a measure of the Syndicate's ability to estimate the ultimate value of claims. Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations, and in 2022 gross and net deteriorations occurred. Included within net claims incurred of GBP 5.7m (2021: GBP 120.9m) is a favourable development of GBP 20.5m (2021: deterioration of GBP 0.8m pre LPT) to claims reserves established at the prior year end.
data.standardized_narrative: For the 2022 financial year, Syndicate 1861 experienced a mixed prior year development, resulting in a net gross strengthening of GBP 7.156m. This was driven by a release of GBP 5.034m on the 2019 underwriting year and a strengthening of GBP 12.190m on the 2020 underwriting year, as calculated from the gross claims development table. The report also notes a net favourable development of GBP 20.5m for prior year end reserves in 2022, and a net deterioration of GBP 0.8m in 2021. General causal factors mentioned include economic inflation, geopolitical events, and changes in the legal environment.
raw_causal_phrases: Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations
in 2022 gross and net deteriorations occurred
rapid increase in inflation, exacerbated by the effects of the war in Ukraine, is impacting insurers and reinsurers, driving up the cost of claims as well as other expenses
data.data_quality_notes: The report provides a net prior year development figure of -GBP 20.5m (favourable development) in Note 9, which differs from the gross prior year development of +GBP 7.156m calculated from the claims development triangle. The gross figure from the triangle is used as per instructions. Percentages for gross premium mix are calculated based on the total gross premiums written.
